gaps.sentence: The ___ majority voted against the proposal.
gaps.explanation: 'An overwhelming majority' = far more than half.

gaps.sentence: All ___ must wear identity badges at all times on site.
gaps.explanation: 'Personnel' = the employees of an organisation; 'personal' is an adjective.

gaps.sentence: You ___ a lot of water by having such long showers.
gaps.hint: to use something valuable without needing to
gaps.explanation: 'Waste' means to use more than necessary; 'save' means the opposite — to avoid using.

gaps.sentence: Should any dispute ___, the matter will go to arbitration.
gaps.explanation: 'Arise' = (problems, disputes) occur; 'rise' means go up and 'raise' needs an object.

gaps.sentence: The two brothers are ___ in appearance but not in character.
gaps.explanation: 'They are alike' — 'alike' follows the verb and cannot come before a noun.

gaps.sentence: The museum is open daily ___ Mondays.
gaps.explanation: 'Except' means not including; 'accept' is a verb meaning to take willingly.

gaps.sentence: Our team has a good ___ of winning on Saturday.
gaps.hint: pattern: have a good ___ of doing something
gaps.explanation: 'Have a chance of doing something' is the standard collocation for the likelihood of success.

gaps.sentence: The committee acted on legal ___ before revising the clause.
gaps.explanation: 'Advice' is the noun; 'advise' is the verb.
